No, first-year residents at Hôtel-Dieu de France largely did not follow prevention rules, with only 5.50% meeting international physical activity guidelines, 25.69% smoking, and just 23% having complete up-to-date immunization.
Among 109 residents (2005–2008), 69.73% skipped meals and 12.84% drank alcohol regularly, while immunization gaps were mainly for MMR and dT Polio.
Hepatitis B immunization was better, with 90.83% fully immunized and 71.56% having an adequate response.
However, the study was not nationally representative, so these findings apply to this hospital's residents rather than all Lebanese future doctors.
No, hypoalbuminemia was not an independent prognostic factor in patients with gastric cancer in this study; albumin lost significance after adjustment for stage, treatment, and CRP.

The study included patients with gastric carcinoma at a Glasgow upper GI surgical unit from April 1997 to December 2005 who had pretreatment albumin and CRP measurements, most with stage III/IV disease receiving palliative treatment, and 157 (72%) died during follow-up.

On univariate analysis albumin was a significant predictor of survival (p<0.001), but on multivariate analysis only stage, treatment, and CRP remained significant (p<0.001), while albumin was no longer an independent predictor.

The evidence is mixed: case-mix reimbursement stimulates hospitals to establish care programmes using process-oriented performance measures, but it has not yet shifted care delivery from function to process.

In a 2007/2008 survey of all Dutch hospitals, structural equation modelling found that adopting case-mix reimbursement within hospital budgeting processes prompted care programmes based on process-oriented performance measures.
However, implementation of those care programmes was not accompanied by a change in focus from independent care activities (function) to a chain of interdependent care activities (process).
Yes, scale matters: the proportion and location of significant racial disparities in breast cancer mortality changed depending on the geographic level and the type of statistic used.

In Texas from 1995-2005, African-American and Hispanic women generally had higher mortality than White non-Hispanic women, with significant disparities especially in southeast metropolitan areas and the southwest border.

Comparing census tract, zip code, and county scales and relative risk (RR) versus risk difference (RD) statistics, the largest proportion of significant results was observed for the RD statistic and census tract data.
Geographic regions with significant disparities for African-Americans and Hispanics frequently had a poverty rate above 10.00%.
Yes, perspective-taking instruction increased standardized patient satisfaction in all three randomized studies among student-clinicians.

Across 608 students randomized to perspective-taking versus neutral instruction before clinical skills examinations, intervention students outscored controls on SP satisfaction in Study 1 (P =.01, effect size 0.16), Study 2 (P =.001, effect size 0.31), and Study 3 (P =.009, effect size 0.13).

The benefit was seen in African American SPs in Study 2, but in Study 3 it appeared only among students with high baseline perspective-taking tendencies (P =.0004, effect size 0.25) and not those with low baseline tendencies (P =.72, effect size 0.00).
Yes, based on patient satisfaction, primary angioplasty appears to be an acceptable alternative to thrombolysis, though the evidence does not address clinical outcomes.

In eight English hospitals, overall satisfaction was high and not significantly different between angioplasty-based intervention and thrombolysis-based control sites (78% vs 71% rated care 'excellent', P=0.074).

Angioplasty sites scored higher for speed of treatment (80% vs 67% 'excellent', P=0.001), while carers rated convenience of visiting lower (12% vs 1% 'poor', P=0.001) but accepted this added inconvenience in the context of a life-saving treatment.
Thus, the passages show acceptability in terms of satisfaction but do not compare clinical efficacy or safety.

No, fluctuating PSA levels are not reassuring enough to avoid biopsy, because cancer detection did not differ significantly between patients with fluctuating PSA and those with steadily increasing PSA.

In a study of 211 patients who underwent at least a second biopsy after a first negative prostate biopsy, 82 had fluctuating PSA (defined as at least one PSA value lower than the preceding one) and 129 had steadily increasing PSA.

There were no significant differences between the groups in cancer detection, clinical or pathological stage, although the steadily increasing PSA group with cancer had a higher Gleason score, and no difference in PSA slope was found between fluctuating-PSA patients with and without cancer.
No, the available evidence suggests decompressive surgery is not effective for cervical spinal cord sarcoidosis accompanied by compressive myelopathy.

In a retrospective series of 12 surgical patients, postoperative recovery rates at 1 week and 4 weeks were -7.4% and -1.1%, respectively, and only 5 patients improved before worsening again at an average of 7.4 weeks after surgery.

Compared with 8 nonsurgical patients treated with high-dose steroids, the JOA score recovery rate after steroid therapy was significantly better in the nonsurgery group (62.5%) than in the surgery group (18.6%, P<0.01).
Yes, pelvic ultrasound appears useful for diagnosing constipation in children, but its role in follow-up is mixed.

In 35 constipated children (mean age 6.8 ± 2.9 years) versus 31 controls (mean age 8.4 ± 3.8 years) by Rome III criteria, posturination rectal diameter was greater in constipated children (3.02 ± 1.04 cm vs 1.98 ± 0.64 cm, P<.001), with a 2.44 cm cutoff (71% sensitive; 76% specific; AUC 0.825; P<.001).
Measurements were reproducible between two radiologists (r = 0.981; P<.001), and rectal anterior wall thickness and fecal load were higher in constipated patients (P<.001).

After one month of treatment, constipation score and fecal load decreased significantly (P<.001), but rectal diameter remained elevated (2.71 ± 0.77 cm) and did not reach normal limits (P>.05), so ultrasound may help monitor fecal load but not normalize rectal diameter during follow-up.
Evidence is mixed: only impetigo contagiosum was increased in children with atopic dermatitis, whereas molluscum contagiosum and herpes virus infection were not.
In a population-based cross-sectional study of 913 children aged 0–6 years (132 with AD), a history of IC, MC, or HI was reported in 45.1%, 19.7%, and 2.5%, respectively.

Multiple logistic regression showed AD children had 1.8 times higher odds of a history of IC than non-AD children, but MC history was significantly correlated with male gender rather than AD, and no correlated factors were found for HI.
Yes—evidence suggests there are different levels of risk for transition to psychosis by UHR criteria, with risk increasing from Trait alone to APS to BLIPS.
In 817 UHR patients at the PACE clinic (Orygen Youth Health, 2000–2008), baseline presentations were 83% APS, 27% Trait, and 4% BLIPS.
When APS alone and APS+Trait were combined, adjusted analysis showed transition risk increased in the order Trait alone < APS < BLIPS (p=0.024).

No, minimal access major surgery in newborns did not hurt less in the only supplied study, which found no significant difference in opioid consumption or pain scores compared with conventional open surgery.
In a retrospective cohort of neonates with esophageal atresia (EA) or congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH), 24 MAS patients (14 EA, 10 CDH) were matched to 48 controls (28 EA, 20 CDH).

At 24 hours, cumulative opioid doses (median mg/kg (IQR)) were 0.84 (0.61-1.83) for MAS vs 1.06 (0.60-1.36) for controls in CDH (p=1.0), and 0.48 (0.30-0.75) for MAS vs 0.49 (0.35-0.79) for controls in EA (p=0.83), with no significant differences at 12, 24, 48 hours, or 7 days, and the same held for postoperative pain scores.
Thus, the evidence indicates MAS does not reduce postoperative pain in this neonatal population.
Yes—after adjustment for age and race, adult waist and hip circumferences scale positively with height.

In NHANES III, among 7,422 men and 7,999 nonpregnant women, waist and hip circumference scaled to height with powers of 0.76 ± 0.08 and 0.45 ± 0.05 in men and 0.80 ± 0.05 and 0.53 ± 0.04 in women, respectively (all P<0.001), and incremental increases were 0.2 to 0.5 cm per centimeter of height.
However, the univariate circumference-height models were weak or nonsignificant, so the association is evident primarily in age- and race-adjusted models.
Yes, but the evidence supports only a limited, selected role for fondaparinux in perioperative bridging.

The summary states that fondaparinux may have a role in bridge therapy for patients in whom low-molecular-weight heparin or inpatient i.v. unfractionated heparin is not possible, contraindicated, or has limited efficacy, such as those with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia or antithrombin III deficiency.

However, guidelines give minimal direction, its 17-21 hour half-life complicates perioperative use, and professional anesthesia guidelines conflict on timing with neuraxial catheters, so it may be optimal to avoid fondaparinux before surgery.

The supporting data are limited: surgical VTE prophylaxis trials used fondaparinux 2.5 mg daily and mostly avoided it before neuraxial anesthesia, and only three case reports described perioperative bridging, one at 2.5 mg and two at a full 7.5 mg treatment dose.
No.
In 32 human milk specimens from 21 HPV-positive and 11 HPV-negative mothers, no high-risk HPV types (16, 18, 31, 33, 35, 39, 45, 51, 52, 56, 58, or 58) DNA was detected by PCR.
These data therefore show no detection of high-risk HPV in human breast milk in this sample.

Yes, teaching medical students to investigate medication errors changed their attitudes toward patient safety, as curriculum effectiveness was demonstrated by significant changes on patient safety attitude questionnaire items.

In this study, 108 medical students during a paediatric clerkship viewed an online video, saw a faculty demonstration of the Learning From Defects tool for a medication administration error, and then identified and analysed medication errors in clinical rotations.

All 25 student groups identified, analysed, and presented patient safety concerns, and the majority felt the curriculum was relevant to their clinical rotation and should remain part of the clerkship.
No, in this study increased patient awareness through educational interventions did not improve accrual into cancer-related clinical trials.

New patients referred to a cancer center over a 4-month period received an orientation session, a pamphlet, and a clinical trials Web site reference, and patient satisfaction with information significantly increased after the interventions.

However, there was no increase in subsequent enrollment in clinical trials, although patients who indicated an inclination to participate tended to have greater satisfaction with the information they received.
No, baseline pain intensity did not predict a poor opioid response in this study: no correlation was found between baseline pain intensity categories and opioid response.

The analysis included 167 patients referred for treatment of cancer-related pain, whose admission pain intensity was classified as mild, moderate, or severe and whose opioid response after dose titration was classified into four levels from good control with minimal escalation to poor control with adverse effects.
The response distribution was 76, 44, 41, and 6 patients for responses a, b, c, and d, respectively, with no correlation between baseline pain intensity and opioid response.
Yes—low performance relative to classmates on year 2 preclerkship clinical performance examinations (CPEs) was a strong predictor of failing the senior CPE.

In a retrospective case-control study of 412 students from the classes of 2005–2010 at a midwestern medical school, year 2 CPE performance (four exams using 12 standardized patient cases total) was compared with passing or failing a year 4 senior CPE.

The study reported that low year 2 CPE performance relative to the class strongly predicted senior CPE failure, whereas USMLE Step 1 scores correlated with senior CPE performance but were considerably weaker predictors.
The supplied passages do not provide the actual sensitivity, specificity, odds ratio, or relative risk values.
Yes—the Turkish EQ-5D showed construct validity in acute coronary syndrome patients, based on its relationships with the MacNew heart-related quality of life scale.
In 122 ACS patients (mean age 62.9±9.3 years; 72.1% male), the EQ-5D index correlated with MacNew subscales at r=0.557–0.721, and the EQ-5D VAS correlated at r=0.297–0.484 (p<0.001 for all).
MacNew global score was also a significant factor for the EQ-5D index (β=0.188; 95% CI 0.152–0.224; p<0.001).
These data support validity for this Turkish version in ACS, but they do not establish validity for other language versions or other measurement properties.
No, this study found no statistically significant difference in laminoplasty outcomes between patients with degenerative cervical stenotic myelopathy and those with segmental OPLL.
In a retrospective review of 40 instrumented laminoplasty cases for cervical myelopathy without kyphosis, 12 had degenerative stenosis and 28 had segmental OPLL.

Both groups showed a significant improvement of more than one Nurick grade after surgery, and the improvement was not statistically different between groups (p>0.05); estimated blood loss (206 vs 155 ml), length of stay (3.7 vs 4 days), VAS neck pain, complication rates, and radiographic loss of extension range of motion also did not differ significantly (p>0.05).
Yes, pelvic pain is associated with defecatory symptoms in women with pelvic organ prolapse.
In a cross-sectional study of 248 women with stage II POP or greater, those stratified into pain versus no-pain groups had significantly more common defecatory symptoms.

Specifically, straining with bowel movement (OR 2.4, 95% CI 1.3–4.6), sense of incomplete emptying (OR 4.4, 95% CI 2.3–8.2), pain with bowel movement (OR 5.3, 95% CI 1.2–23.0), and splinting with bowel movement (OR 3.8, 95% CI 2.0–7.5) were more common in women with pelvic pain.

Bottom line: the evidence is mixed—PET/CT does not add to MDCT/MR for hepatic staging but may help in selected extrahepatic sites, though it also produced incorrect additional findings. In a prospective study of 97 patients evaluated for resection of liver metastases from colorectal carcinoma, sensitivity for hepatic staging was significantly higher with MDCT/MR than PET/CT (89.2% vs 55%, p < 0.001). PET/CT was superior to MDCT/MR only for detecting locoregional recurrence (p = 0.03) and recurrence in uncommon sites (p = 0.016). PET/CT findings changed therapeutic strategy in 17 patients, but the additional information was correct in only 8 and wrong in 9.
The evidence is insufficient to conclude that ADMA levels in young adults born preterm predict early endothelial dysfunction.

In a study of 32 ex-ELBW adults aged 17–29 years (mean 22.2 ± 2.3) compared with 25 healthy term controls, the study reported a significant ADMA difference between groups (0.606±0.095 vs 0.562±0.101 μmol/L, p<0.05) and inverse correlations with gestational age (r=-0.61, p<0.00001) and birth weight (r=-0.57, p<0.0002).

The passages note that preterm birth/low birth weight are later cardiovascular risk factors and that high ADMA is associated with adverse cardiovascular events, but they do not measure endothelial dysfunction.
Thus, these data show ADMA differences and correlations in ex-ELBW adults, not that ADMA predicts early endothelial dysfunction.

No, the supplied evidence suggests xanthogranulomatous cholecystitis (XGC) is not a premalignant condition, based on molecular markers that resemble chronic cholecystitis rather than gallbladder carcinoma (GBC).

In a study of 65 XGC, 69 GBC, 18 chronic cholecystitis, and 10 control gallbladders, p53 was positive in 3% of XGC versus 52% of GBC and none in chronic cholecystitis/control, while PCNA was positive in 11% of XGC versus 65% of GBC and none in chronic cholecystitis/control.
Beta-catenin was positive in all groups, but XGC, chronic cholecystitis, and control showed homogeneous membranous staining, whereas GBC showed altered cytoplasmic/nuclear staining.
These findings indicate a benign molecular profile for XGC, but the passages do not provide direct follow-up data on malignant transformation.

Yes, mitochondria play a role in remodelling lace plant leaves during PCD, as indicated by cyclosporine A treatment reducing perforations and producing non-PCD-like mitochondrial dynamics. In Aponogeton madagascariensis window-stage leaves, mitochondrial dynamics were classified into four stages (M1–M4) based on distribution, motility, and membrane potential, and a TUNEL assay showed fragmented nDNA in a gradient across these stages. Compared with controls, in vivo cyclosporine A treatment resulted in significantly fewer leaf perforations and mitochondrial dynamics similar to those of non-PCD cells.

The evidence is insufficient to conclude that the improvements in gynaecological cancer survival in Anglia were an effect of centralisation of care and multidisciplinary management, although the study found a temporal association consistent with that hypothesis.
In about 2.3 million people in the Anglia Cancer Network, 3,406 gynaecological cancer cases from 1996 to 2003 were analysed.

Survival was broadly unchanged for 1996-1999 diagnoses but improved for 2000-2003 diagnoses (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.64-0.79 versus 1996-1999), with a concurrent shift toward major surgery in specialist centres after 2000.
Adjustment for treatments or follow-up method did not attenuate the improvement, but the passages do not isolate centralisation or multidisciplinary management as the cause.
The evidence is insufficient to say dogs can prime autistic children for therapy, because the supplied study only shows behavioral modulation during sessions, not priming for later therapy.

It rests on a single 12-year-old boy with autism spectrum disorder who was compared between one-to-one structured activities with a therapist assisted by a certified therapy dog and the same therapist alone.

In the presence of the dog, the boy showed more frequent and longer positive behaviors, such as smiling and positive physical contacting, and less frequent and shorter negative behaviors, such as aggressive manifestations.
However, the passage notes only limited studies and much anecdotal literature and does not test whether dogs prepare or prime children for therapy.

The evidence is insufficient to conclude that combining antiretroviral agents in a single dosage form enhances quality of life: in a cost-utility study, fixed dose combination (FXD) yielded a mean utility gain of 0.085 over multiple free dose combination (FRC), but the difference was not statistically significant.
The study compared HIV/AIDS patients with ≥2 active antiretroviral medications on FXD versus FRC, matching 70 FXD patients 1:1 to FRC patients.

Although FXD had higher mean annual cost ($15,766.15 vs $11,875.21) and an ICUR of $45,540.49/QALY, with >50% probability of being cost-effective above $40,000, the quality-of-life gain did not reach significance.

The evidence is mixed and domain-specific: improvements in clinical services most consistently predict reductions in under-5 mortality, while outreach and family/community measures show only some associations.
In 27 high-burden countries (with a 19-country African subset), changes in coverage of clinical, outreach, and family/community services were correlated with changes in under-5 mortality rates.

In the outreach domain, antenatal care and family planning were significantly correlated with mortality decline, but immunization was not.

In the family/community domain, breastfeeding improvements were associated in the 30 countries but not the African subset, whereas nutritional status improvements were associated in African countries.
Yes, endometrial polyp formation is associated with increased expression of both VEGF and TGF-β1, though the increase is compartment- and phase-specific.

In a prospective study of 70 premenopausal women comparing polyps with adjacent endometrium, VEGF was significantly higher in glandular cells in both proliferative (P<0.001) and secretory (P=0.03) phases and in stromal cells only in the proliferative phase (P=0.006).
TGF-β1 was significantly higher in glandular cells only in the proliferative phase (P=0.02) and in stromal cells in both proliferative (P=0.006) and secretory (P=0.008) phases.

Consulting both sources identified up to 56% more accidents and up to 46% more convictions than either source alone.
The evidence is mixed: in a cross-sectional study, older cancer patients had specific needs but few significant differences from younger patients, except for intimacy and support.

Older patients most often requested financial-insurance information (73.9%), talking with people with the same illness (71.7%), more comprehensible information from doctors/nurses (71.7%), and better dialogue with clinicians (69.6%), yet only intimacy and support needs differed significantly between age groups.

The evidence is mixed: in a post hoc analysis of an RCT, the unadjusted adenoma detection rate (ADR) was higher with Golytely (26.2%, 27/103) than MiraLAX (16.1%, 14/87), but this difference was not statistically significant (P=0.091), whereas multivariate analysis found Golytely 2.28 times more likely to be associated with adenoma detection (95% CI 1.05–4.98, P=0.04).
The population was 190 average-risk screening colonoscopy patients prospectively enrolled (87 MiraLAX, 103 Golytely).
Thus the passages show a significant adjusted association but a non-significant unadjusted ADR comparison, so they do not settle a simple yes/no.
The evidence is insufficient to show that growth hormone replacement reduces mortality in adults with growth hormone deficiency.
In a Dutch nationwide registry of adults with GHD, the treatment group (n=2229) had 95 deaths versus 74.6 expected, with an all-cause standardized mortality ratio of 1.27 (95% CI 1.04-1.56).

Untreated primary (n=109) and partly treated secondary control (n=356) groups had mortality not different from the background population, but the effect of GH treatment on mortality remains to be established.
Yes, trauma center level made a difference for mortality among severely injured trauma patients in this Australian health service.

In 1,986 trauma presentations with Injury Severity Score >15 from 2002–2007, patients presenting to a level III trauma center had a significantly higher risk of death than those presenting to the level I center, regardless of age, sex, ISS, or prehospital time.
The study was also designed to assess hospital length of stay, but the supplied results report only the mortality difference.

Yes—this study found several prognostic factors in type 1 hepatorenal syndrome (HRS) that may be underrecognized, including ESLD etiology, higher serum creatinine, and urinary sodium 6–10 mEq/L at therapy initiation.

In 68 patients with type 1 HRS who were not liver transplant candidates and were treated with albumin, midodrine/octreotide, pressors, and hemodialysis, median survival was 13 days, and survival differed by ESLD etiology: autoimmune 49 days, cardiac cirrhosis 22 days, idiopathic 15.5 days, viral 15 days, hepatitis C plus alcohol 14.5 days, alcohol 8 days, and neoplasia 4 days (p=0.048).

In 246 patients with NPC and lung metastasis alone at diagnosis or as first failure after primary treatment (1993–2008), median post-metastasis survival was 45.6 vs 23.7 months and median overall survival was 73.7 vs 46.2 months for combined therapy vs chemotherapy alone (P<0.001).
Independent prognostic factors were age, disease-free interval, and treatment modality for overall survival, while only age and treatment modality remained independent for post-metastasis survival.
Stratified analysis showed combined therapy benefited patients with DFI >1 year but not those with DFI ≤1 year.

The evidence is insufficient to say whether remote ischemic postconditioning protects against ischemic damage in percutaneous coronary revascularization, because the supplied passages describe only the objective and methods of a trial and report no results.

The trial randomized 320 patients undergoing elective PCI for stable angina or non-ST elevation acute coronary syndrome with troponin <1 ng/ml to three 5-min cycles of arm-cuff ischemia at 200 mm Hg versus an uninflated cuff placebo.

Its prespecified primary outcome was the maximum troponin increase in the first 24 h, and secondary outcomes were heart failure readmission or cardiovascular mortality at 1 year, with a diabetic population also studied.
Thus, the passages do not show whether postconditioning reduced troponin or improved clinical outcomes.

The evidence is mixed and limited: in a small pilot RCT, a preoperative medically supervised weight management (MSWM) program did not improve weight loss after laparoscopic adjustable gastric banding (LAGB), though it may have improved postoperative physical activity.

The trial randomized 55 publicly insured patients meeting NIH bariatric surgery criteria, with complete follow-up on 23, to a 6-month MSWM program with monthly visits or usual care; MSWM participants attended an average of 2 sessions preoperatively.
Postoperatively, there were no significant differences in weight loss or most patient behaviors between groups, but MSWM participation appeared to have a positive effect on physical activity.
Thus, the passages do not show a clear overall improvement in bariatric surgery outcomes; they show no weight-loss benefit and a possible activity benefit in a very small pilot sample.

No—delivery mode was not significantly associated with postpartum quality of life in this rural Chinese sample. In the Swiss National Cohort of all residents over age 44 (n=2,440,242), being married benefited men more than women, and among 45–64-year-olds the highest mortality risks were for divorced men living alone (HR 1.72, 95% CI 1.67–1.76) and single men living alone (HR 1.67, 95% CI 1.63–1.71), whereas women in that age group had the highest risk if single and living with a partner (HR 1.70, 95% CI 1.58–1.82).

Yes, an advance care planning model was feasible to embed into the organizational structures of community palliative care services.

Yes—there was a differential in dental health among new recruits to the British Armed Forces, with Army recruits having significantly more dental decay and greater treatment resource need than Royal Navy or Royal Air Force recruits.

In 32 rabbits (3–5.5 months old, 3000–4200 g) undergoing laparotomy with total gastrectomy and splenectomy under ketamine+xylazine, different preoperative fasting periods were used (minimum 2 hours absolute fasting; maximum 8.5 hours for liquids and 20.5 hours for solids).

Despite this fasting, all animals had gastric content at the end of surgery and mean blood glucose rose from 199.4 mg/dl to 326.1 mg/dl, with a moderate negative correlation between liquid/solid fasting and the amount of solid gastric content.
Mortality was 3.125% (1/32) and morbidity was 6.25% (2/32).

The evidence is insufficient to say whether mesopic pupil size can be measured with a cobalt blue light slit-lamp biomicroscopy method, because the supplied study describes a slit-lamp biomicroscopy-based method (SLBM) for pupil diameter but does not specify mesopic conditions or cobalt blue light.

Thus the passages show SLBM can measure pupil diameter but do not settle the specific question about mesopic pupil size using cobalt blue light.

Yes, instrumental activities of daily living (IADL) disability predicted dementia at both 1- and 2-year follow-up in a multicenter prospective cohort study in European memory clinics. The study included individuals aged 55 and older without dementia, measuring IADLs from five informant-based questionnaires and adjusting for age, sex, education, depression, Mini-Mental State Examination, and verbal memory. The distribution of health care benefits in Kenya did not meet the principles of universal coverage because benefits were distributed on the basis of ability to pay and not on need for care.

In two nationally representative household surveys from 2003 and 2007, the three sectors had similar pro-rich distribution in 2003, but in 2007 the private-not-for-profit sector was pro-poor, the public sector was equal, and the private-for-profit sector remained pro-rich.
Larger pro-rich disparities were recorded for inpatient compared with outpatient benefits at the hospital level, while primary health care services were pro-poor.
Thus, the evidence shows some pro-poor components but an overall distribution that did not meet universal coverage principles.
Yes, serum can be used for analyzing EGFR mutation status in patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer, based on high concordance with matched tumor samples.

In 57 patients with advanced NSCLC, EGFR mutations were detected in 11 serum samples and 12 tumor samples, with concordant serum-tumor status in 50 of 57 pairs (87.7%) and a correlation index of 0.62 (P<0.001).

Response to EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors was significantly associated with EGFR mutations in both tumor and serum samples (P<0.05), although overall survival did not differ significantly by mutation status in either sample type (P>0.05).
Yes for breast and colorectal cancer, but the supplied passages do not report whether distance is a barrier for lung cancer.

In 3,917 Washington State Medicaid patients with breast, colorectal, or lung cancer from 1997-2003, driving distance and time to primary care were tested against stage at diagnosis and time to treatment.
Later-stage breast cancer diagnosis was associated with travel burden (OR 1.488 per 100 driving miles, P=.037; OR 1.270 per driving hour, P=.016).
Longer time-to-treatment after colorectal cancer diagnosis was also associated with travel burden (14.57 days per 100 driving miles, P=.002; 5.86 days per driving hour, P=.018).
No lung cancer-specific association is given in the passages.

No, though the evidence is limited by a retrospective design and small sample of 35 patients, no spinal haematoma, meningitis, or epidural abscess occurred with epidural analgesia during HIPEC with oxaliplatin or cisplatin.
Norepinephrine was required in 2 patients (6%) peroperatively and 4 patients (11%) in the first postoperative 24 hours.
Five patients (14%) had thrombopenia or prothrombin time <60% before catheter removal, but no thrombopenia or coagulation disorders were recorded on the day of catheter removal.
Thus, major neuraxial complications were absent in this series, but haemodynamic and coagulation concerns remain.

No, performance in selection processes did not predict performance as a dental student in this study. The finding rests on a longitudinal review of admissions data for students entering dental education at the University of Otago, New Zealand, between 2004 and 2009, compared with academic performance throughout the dental programme. After controlling for variables, pre-admission academic average, UMAT scores, and structured interview performance did not predict performance as a dental student. Instead, class place in second year was a strong predictor of final-year class place, and the best predictors of higher final-year class placement were New Zealand European ethnicity and domestic rather than international student status.
Conditionally yes: the IADPSG criteria were cost-effective only when postdelivery care reduces diabetes incidence.

In a decision-analysis model of pregnant women screened for GDM, the IADPSG strategy versus current standard screening gained 6,178 QALYs per 100,000 women screened at a cost of $125,633,826, with an ICER of $20,336 per QALY gained.
When postdelivery care was not accomplished, the IADPSG strategy was no longer cost-effective, and results were robust in sensitivity analyses.
Yes, in an in vivo pig model laser pretreatment enhanced transdermal lidocaine absorption.
In four pigs, serum lidocaine and MEGX were undetectable in untreated skin, but both became detectable after Er:YAG laser treatment before topical 4% lidocaine application.
Peak lidocaine was significantly higher at 250 µm (0.62 mg/L) than at 500 µm (0.45 mg/L), 50 µm (0.48 mg/L), or 25 µm (0.3 mg/L).
Peak MEGX was also significantly higher at 250 µm (0.048 mg/L) than at 500 µm (0.018 mg/L), 50 µm (0.036 mg/L), or 25 µm (0.0144 mg/L).
Yes—in a rabbit expander model, partial expander deflation immediately before radiotherapy was associated with aggravated chronic radiodermatitis and increased capsule thickness.

The study used 18 New Zealand rabbits with 250-cc anatomic breast expanders; Group I received radiotherapy with full expanders, Group II had partial deflation immediately before radiotherapy, and a control group received no radiotherapy.

Partial deflation in Group II significantly increased skin blood flow, and histopathology showed aggravated epidermal atrophy, dermal inflammation and fibrosis, neovascularisation, vascular changes, and increased capsule thickness, especially around the lower expander pole.
This evidence comes from an animal model rather than direct human two-stage breast reconstruction data.

The evidence is insufficient to conclude that pictorial warning labels can address smoking-related health disparities, because the only relevant study examined content effectiveness and moderation by education rather than disparity reduction.

In field experiments with 529 adult smokers and 530 young adults (258 nonsmokers; 271 smokers), pictorial HWLs with didactic text had equivalent or significantly higher credibility, relevance, and impact than testimonial forms.

However, responses differed by educational attainment: didactic forms were consistently rated higher among participants with higher education, whereas the difference between didactic and testimonial forms was weaker or not statistically significant among participants with lower education.

The study also found graphic imagery of diseased organs was rated higher in credibility, relevance, and impact than imagery of human suffering, but it did not test whether these labels reduce smoking-related health disparities.
The evidence is insufficient to definitively answer whether prophylactic antibiotics are necessary, though it suggests the early infection rate is low without routine prophylaxis.
In a retrospective series of 1,183 totally implantable venous access device placements, CLABSIs occurred in 7 patients (0.6%) within 30 days.
At placement, 81 patients (7%) were receiving antibiotics incidental to the procedure, and one of these developed a CLABSI.
No direct comparison of prophylactic versus no prophylactic antibiotics was reported, so these data do not settle necessity.
Yes—a four-diagram instruction manual enabled most laypersons to insert and ventilate with the Laryngeal Mask Supreme® in a manikin pilot study.

Among 150 laypersons, 145 (96.7%) inserted the device in the right direction, and 119 (79.3%) achieved tidal volumes greater than 150 mL within 2 minutes, with a mean time to insertion and first ventilation of 83.2 ± 29 s.
Success did not differ significantly by previous BLS training, technical education, or gender.
This single-arm manikin study supports feasibility but does not compare the manual against other instructions or assess use in real patients.
Bottom line: The evidence indicates no consistent correlation between DaTSCAN findings in essential tremor and Parkinson's disease; ET patients typically lack the dopaminergic deficit seen in PD.

In 28 ET patients versus 28 normal volunteers, visual SPECT interpretation showed no uptake differences, while semiquantitative analysis found reduced striatal uptake in ET, and PD patients had reduced putamen uptake.
Clinical follow-up of 20 ET patients showed no signs of PD, and follow-up DaTSCAN in 10 was negative in all but one with an equivocal baseline that deteriorated 12 months later.
Thus, DaTSCAN primarily helps differentiate ET from PD rather than demonstrating a correlation with PD.
The evidence is mixed: composite process-indicator scores were not consistently associated with short-term outcomes across all levels and cancer types.

In 4,732 elective colon carcinoma patients and 2,239 rectum carcinoma patients from 85 Dutch hospitals, five composite measures were compared with risk-adjusted postoperative mortality and morbidity at patient and hospital levels.

At the patient level, only one composite measure was negatively associated with morbidity for rectum carcinoma, whereas at the hospital level strong negative associations were found with mortality and morbidity for rectum carcinoma (p<0.05) and with morbidity for colon carcinoma.
No, site of access did not significantly influence early outcomes after endovenous laser ablation for small saphenous varicose veins.

In 59 patients with unilateral saphenopopliteal junction incompetence and small saphenous vein reflux, access above mid-calf (n=33) versus below mid-calf (n=26) showed no significant differences in complications (phlebitis 6% vs 3.8%, P>.05; paresthesia 6% vs 19%, P=.223) or recurrence (9% vs 3.8%, P=.623).
Both groups had significant improvements in VCSS, AVVQ, SF-36, and EuroQol scores up to 1 year (P<.05).
Yes—the supplied study indicates that horizontal canal ocular reflex is influenced by gravity-related/otolith input.

In seven healthy humans, ice-water stimulation of the right ear produced nystagmus analyzed with three-dimensional video-oculography while subjects were repositioned through left-ear-down, prone, right-ear-down, and supine positions at 20 s intervals.

Eye movements in supine versus prone positions were not symmetric, and nystagmus in left-ear-down versus right-ear-down positions was not symmetric, indicating the eyeball rotation axis was affected by the shift in gravity direction on the head.

Yes—in young obese males, carotid pulsatility and resistance indexes were significantly higher than in healthy controls, supporting them as early sonographic markers of obesity-related vascular dysfunction.

The evidence comes from a study of 35 young obese males and 23 age-matched healthy male volunteers in whom common carotid artery pulsatility index and resistance index were calculated from pulsed Doppler blood flow velocity curves.

Mean pulsatility index and resistance index were statistically higher in obese subjects than controls, alongside higher BMI, waist circumference, blood pressure, insulin resistance, and inflammatory markers.
No, late-night salivary cortisol was not a better screening test than standard tests in this population; its specificity was significantly lower than 24-hour UFC.

In 40 obese patients with Type 2 diabetes and no clinical features of Cushing's syndrome, specificities were 70% (95% CI 53-83%) for late-night salivary cortisol (cutoff 10 nmol/L), 90% (76-97%) for 24-hour UFC (400 nmol), and 72% (55-85%) for 1 mg DST (50 nmol/L).
Late-night salivary cortisol specificity was significantly less than 24-hour UFC (P=0.039) but not significantly different from 1 mg DST (P>0.99).
The evidence is mixed: Indigenous Australians show a 5-7 year earlier life expectancy equivalence but no consistent 20-year lead in age-associated conditions.

At age 63 for women and age 65 for men, Indigenous people had the same life expectancy as non-Indigenous people at age 70, while there is no consistent pattern of a 20-year lead in age-specific prevalence of age-associated conditions.

Some conditions like diabetes are highly prevalent from middle age, but others show little or no lead, suggesting premature aging occurs but not uniformly or to the degree implied by aged care policy.
The radiographic transition zone does correlate with the level of aganglionosis on the specimen, but the agreement is only fair/moderate and not precise.

In 61 reviewed preoperative contrast enemas from 79 patients operated for Hirschsprung's disease, radiographic findings matched the pathology specimen in 8/19 rectal (42%), 20/35 rectosigmoid (57%), all 6 long-segment (100%), and both total colonic cases (100%), with global agreement of 58.1% and κ = 0.39 (CI 0.24–0.57).
No - global management at the same centre did not improve results in this retrospective study.

In 45 GM versus 66 SM patients with synchronous liver metastases and colorectal cancer, overall survival was not significantly different (67% vs 51% at 3 years; 35% vs 31% at 5 years), and 5-year disease-free survival was higher with separate management (14% vs 11%, P=0.009).

Global management reduced the mean number of procedures (1.6 vs 2.3, P=0.003) and more often performed the first liver resection during colorectal surgery (62% vs 6%, P<0.0001), but this did not translate into better oncologic outcomes.
The evidence is insufficient to say whether age moderates the effect of personality disorder on coping style in psychiatric inpatients.
In 238 adult psychiatric inpatients aged 18–100, age and personality traits predicted coping strategies, while personality disorder was not a significant predictor of coping strategies.
Older adults reported lower dysfunctional coping and younger patients had more personality dysfunction, but the study did not report an age-by-personality-disorder interaction.

Yes, micro-computed tomography appears reliable for assessing maxillary alveolar bone microstructure, based on significant positive correlations between micro-CT bone volumetric density (BV/TV) and conventional histomorphometric percentage of bone.
In 39 human maxillary alveolar bone biopsies analyzed by micro-CT, 10 were directly compared with stereologic-based histomorphometry using SEM and optic microscopy.
The correlations were r=0.933 for SEM (P<0.001), r=0.950 for toluidine blue OM (P<0.001), and r=0.667 for dark-field OM (P=0.05).
The passages support reliability for BV/TV and related trabecular parameters but do not report separate validation for every microstructural variable.

Yes, acceptance rates were socially imbalanced, with older persons with high financial assets accepting preventive home visits more frequently than those with low assets (adjusted OR = 1.5, 95% CI 1.1–2.0). This finding comes from 1,023 community dwelling 80-year-old individuals in the Danish intervention study on preventive home visits, where socioeconomic status was measured by financial assets. The association was attenuated when adjusted by municipality invitational procedures, and the odds ratio for acceptance was larger among low-asset persons invited by a letter with a proposed date than among high-asset persons invited by other procedures, though estimates had wide confidence intervals.
Yes, technical factors affect prognosis: selective embolization was independently associated with better survival in multivariate analysis (hazard ratio 0.68; 95% CI 0.48-0.97; p = 0.033).
The study included 815 patients with HCC (Child A or B, five or fewer tumors ≤7 cm, no extrahepatic metastasis) who received embolization as initial treatment at 43 centers.
Univariate analysis also found use of iodized oil and selective embolization to be significantly better prognostic factors.

No, the evidence suggests there is little place for ultrasound as a primary diagnostic test for internal derangement of the temporomandibular joint, because static and dynamic high-resolution ultrasound showed considerably lower sensitivity than magnetic resonance imaging.
This finding comes from a study of 40 patients and 20 asymptomatic volunteers, totaling 120 temporomandibular joints, in which ultrasound was compared with magnetic resonance as the reference test.
The study also reported that articular sounds and physical signs were often insufficient, and that ultrasound faced technical difficulties from limited access due to surrounding bone structures.
Yes—third-trimester ultrasound can predict the presentation of the first twin at delivery, based on high positive predictive values in a retrospective cohort of 238 twin pregnancies.
In that study, 896 sonograms were reviewed and the presentation of twin A on ultrasound at seven gestational-age intervals was compared with presentation at delivery.

The positive predictive value of cephalic presentation for persistent cephalic presentation at delivery reached 95% after 28 weeks, and the positive predictive value for noncephalic presentation at delivery was >90% after 32 weeks.
The passages do not report the actual sensitivity or specificity values, only that they were calculated.
No; in a controlled feeding study, after adjustment for potential confounders, African American women did not require fewer calories than non-African American women to maintain weight.
The analysis included 206 women (73% African American), aged 22-75 years, participating in the DASH trial with prehypertension or stage 1 hypertension.

During feeding, mean calorie intake was 2168 kcal in African American women vs 2073 kcal in non-African American women, 94.7 kcal higher in African American women unadjusted (P<.05), but the adjusted difference was -2.8 kcal (P=.95).

Yes, a porcine training model was developed to teach and practice retroperitoneoscopic nephrectomy. In 15 piglets, a standard retroperitoneoscopic nephrectomy (RPN) training model was performed with three ports, with operative time ranging from 15 to 50 minutes (median 30) and blood loss from 5 to 100 mL (median 20). The experimental learning curve was eight cases, with significant differences between the first eight (group A) and last seven (group B) for peritoneal opening (p = 0.025), operative time (p = 0.0037), and blood loss (p = 0.026). The model simulated the whole procedure from creating the space to nephrectomy completion.

The evidence is mixed and limited to one specialty: in intensive care medicine, open access was associated with a citation advantage in some analyses, but the overall median citation difference was not statistically significant.
Among 161 articles published in Intensive Care Medicine in 2008 (76% non-open access), median citations were 8 (IQR 4-12) for non-open access versus 9 (6-18) for open access (p=0.084).
In the highest citation range (>8), citations were 13 (10-16) versus 18 (13-21) (p=0.008), and average citations per article per month at 30-35 months were 0.28±0.6 versus 0.38±0.7 (p=0.043).
In adjusted analysis, open access status was an independent factor for citation advantage (β=3.618; p=0.006).

The evidence is mixed/insufficient: this retrospective cohort found no decrease in mortality or hospitalization costs with regional versus general anesthesia, and it did not clearly report a morbidity benefit.
Among 308 patients undergoing surgery for hip fracture, 73 received regional anesthesia and 235 received general anesthesia.
Average hospitalization cost was no different ($16,789 vs $16,815, P=0.9557), and in-hospital mortality and readmission rates were not statistically different.
The passages state that postoperative morbidity data were collected but do not report a significant morbidity difference.

Yes, the evidence suggests insulin resistance explains the association between hyperglycemia and cardiovascular risk, because the glucose associations became non-significant after adjustment for insulin sensitivity while insulin sensitivity remained associated. In 60 middle-aged individuals without diabetes, fasting and 2-hour plasma glucose were associated with higher Framingham risk scores (r²=0.21 and 0.24, P<0.001 for both) and insulin sensitivity with lower risk (r²=0.36, P<0.001), but after adjustment for insulin sensitivity and the other glucose measure, fasting glucose (P=0.060) and 2-hour glucose (P=0.143) were no longer significant while insulin sensitivity remained associated (P<0.001). Body fat was not associated with Framingham risk score when insulin sensitivity was taken into account (P=0.550).
The evidence is mixed or insufficient to blame behavioural risk factors, as the study shows associations but not causation.

Among Black South Africans with optimal blood pressure (≤120/80 mm Hg) followed for 5 years, those who became hypertensive smoked more (68.2% vs 49.8%) and had greater baseline waist circumference and γ-glutamyltransferase.
Alcohol intake predicted central systolic blood pressure and carotid cross-sectional wall area at follow-up, and waist circumference predicted blood pressure changes.
However, the observational design cannot establish that these behavioural factors caused the conversion to hypertension.
No, the supplied study does not show vitamin D deficiency as a feature of pediatric celiac disease.

In prepubertal children aged 3–12 years with biopsy-diagnosed CD not on a gluten-free diet (n=24) compared with non-CD children of the same age (n=50), mean 25(OH)D levels did not differ significantly (27.58 +/- 9.91 versus 26.20 +/- 10.45, p = 0.59).

Non-obese CD patients also did not differ from non-obese normal children (28.39 +/- 10.26 versus 30.64 +/- 12.08, p = 0.52), although they had higher 25(OH)D levels than obese normal children (p = 0.009).
Therefore, this study does not support vitamin D deficiency as a general feature of pediatric CD.
No.

In a 2x2 experiment with 106 young male adults, participants in both stress and no-stress conditions consumed substantially more alcohol when confederates drank alcohol than when they drank soda, and there was no difference in alcohol consumed between stress and no-stress conditions.
No moderating effect of stress on the tendency to drink along with peers was found.
The evidence is insufficient to conclude that ultrasound-estimated fetal weight is a modifiable risk factor for cesarean delivery, although it is an independent risk factor in this study.
In a retrospective cohort of 2329 singleton term live births, women with US-EFW within 1 month of delivery had higher CD rates than those without (15.7% vs 10.2%; P<.001).
After adjustment, US-EFW remained an independent risk factor for CD (OR 1.44; 95% CI 1.1-1.9), with higher risk when US-EFW was >3500 g (OR 1.8; 95% CI 1.3-2.7).
However, the passages do not show whether modifying knowledge or use of US-EFW changes CD risk.

No, according to the supplied passage, an increase in the cigarette tax rate was not linked to higher retail prices in China's 2009 excise tax increase. The Chinese State Tobacco Monopoly Administration used its policy authority to ensure that retail cigarette prices did not change despite the tax increase. The tax increase was collected at the producer and wholesale levels, resulting in higher government tax revenue and lower tobacco industry profits, with no increase in the retail price of cigarettes for consumers.

The evidence is insufficient to recommend routine screening of all HIV-infected patients for silent myocardial ischaemia using gated myocardial perfusion SPECT, because in 94 asymptomatic HIV-infected patients the overall positivity was only 9.6% and all positive scans occurred in men older than 52 years with at least two other cardiovascular risk factors.
In that high-risk subgroup of 47 patients, the prevalence of SMI detected by SPECT was 19.2%, and the combination of gender and age was the only independent parameter associated with SMI (p=0.01).
The passages do not show whether screening improves outcomes or is cost-effective, so they do not settle whether all HIV-infected patients should be screened.
No, immediate breast reconstruction did not compromise delivery of adjuvant chemotherapy in this study; there was no significant difference in the median time to chemotherapy.
This comparison included 107 patients who received immediate breast reconstruction and 113 who received mastectomy alone.
Overall complication rates were comparable (35.5% vs 45.1%, p=0.2), although 11.5% of tissue expanders required removal and more seromas occurred in the mastectomy group.
Yes, European people with type 1 diabetes have been reported to consume a high atherogenic diet.

In the EURODIAB Prospective Complications Study, 1102 European patients with type 1 diabetes (553 men, 549 women, baseline age 33 ± 10 years, duration 15 ± 9 years) had dietary data at baseline and after 7 years.

Adherence to European recommendations was poor for saturated fat (11% at baseline, 13% at follow-up) and fibre (1.4%, 2.4%), but moderate for fat (34%, 40%), cholesterol (39%, 47%), and carbohydrate (34%, 41%), and adequate for protein (76%, 78%).
These findings of poor saturated fat and fibre adherence are consistent with a high atherogenic diet.
Yes, obesity at the start of adolescence was associated with greater wheezing prevalence and persistence, but not with incident wheezing.

In the 1993 Pelotas birth cohort followed from ages 11 to 15 years, obese individuals at 11 years had a 50% higher prevalence of wheezing at 15 years than eutrophic individuals (RR 1.53; 95% CI: 1.14-2.05), and the risk of persistent wheezing was 1.82 (95% CI: 1.30-2.54) after controlling for confounders.
Weight status and skinfolds were not associated with incident wheezing.

Yes, surgical effort still matters in quaternary cytoreductive surgery for ovarian cancer, based on the finding that complete macroscopic tumor clearance/no residual disease was associated with longer overall survival.

In 49 epithelial ovarian cancer patients undergoing quaternary cytoreduction, mean overall survival was 43 months (95% CI 26.4-59.5) for patients without any tumour residuals versus 13.4 months (95% CI 7.42-19.4) for those with any residuals (P=0.001).

Multivariate analysis identified multifocal tumour dissemination as predictive of incomplete tumour resection and lower survival, while postoperative systemic chemotherapy had a protective impact on overall survival.
However, this is a single-institution series and does not provide randomized evidence that attempting more extensive surgery itself improves survival.
Yes, the type of tibial component affects mechanical alignment in unicompartmental knee replacement.

In a retrospective review of 89 patients who underwent robotic-guided UKR, those receiving a metal-backed onlay tibial component had mean postoperative mechanical alignment significantly closer to neutral (2.8°, 95% CI 2.4°–3.2°) than those receiving an all-polyethylene inlay component (3.9°, 95% CI 3.4°–4.4°), adjusting for gender, BMI, age, side, and preoperative mechanical alignment (R2=0.65; P=0.003).
The study also found that tibial polyethylene insert thickness significantly affected postoperative alignment when added to the model (R2=0.68; P=0.01).
Thus, evidence from this single study supports an effect of tibial component design on mechanical alignment.
The evidence is insufficient to conclude that etoricoxib is effective for preventing heterotopic ossification after primary total hip arthroplasty.

In a small single-arm phase-2 study of 42 patients receiving oral etoricoxib 90 mg for seven days after cemented primary total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis, 62% had no heterotopic ossification, 31% had Brooker grade 1, and 7% had Brooker grade 2.
Because the study had no control or comparator group and reported no statistical comparison, these results cannot establish efficacy.
Yes, intensive chemotherapy appeared safe for rural patients in this retrospective audit, with serious adverse event rates and dose intensities comparable to urban patients and no toxic deaths.

The study included 121 patients with metastatic colorectal or node-positive breast cancer (68 urban vs 53 rural) who received intensive regimens at the same doses as urban patients, with side effects usually managed locally by rural general practitioners.
Breast cancer dose intensity was >95% in both groups, and rates of febrile neutropenia were 9.3% vs 7.4% (P=0.56); for XELOX, diarrhoea was 20% vs 19% (P=0.66) and vomiting 20% vs 11% (P=0.11).
Only two patients were transferred to Townsville for admission, and no toxic death occurred in either group.

Yes—the sputum OraQuick® HIV-1/2 assay appears promising for screening TB/HIV co-infection, with 90% sensitivity (9/10) and 100% specificity (307/307) compared with serum ELISA among patients diagnosed with tuberculosis.
Its positive predictive value was 100% and negative predictive value was 99.68%.

However, the sensitivity estimate rests on only 10 HIV-positive sputum specimens, and the supplied passages do not confirm that the study was conducted in Central India, so the evidence is promising but not definitive for that setting.
The evidence is insufficient to say whether early second-look tympanoplasty reduces conversion to modified radical mastoidectomy.

In a single-surgeon retrospective series of 132 second-look operations performed at a mean of 6 months after primary surgery, the conversion rate to modified radical mastoidectomy was 3% (4 cases), and 73.1% of recurrent/residual cholesteatoma was easily removed at second look.
However, the study reports only this rate and does not compare early versus delayed second-look surgery or demonstrate a reduction.
Yes, operative treatment was superior to nonoperative treatment for displaced midshaft clavicular fractures in a meta-analysis of four randomized controlled trials.

In 321 patients, operative treatment had lower rates of nonunion (95% CI 0.05–0.43, P=0.0004), malunion (95% CI 0.06–0.34, P<0.00001), and overall complications (95% CI 0.43–0.76, P=0.0001) than nonoperative treatment.

Operative treatment also had lower rates of neurologic symptoms (95% CI 0.20–0.74, P=0.004) and dissatisfaction with appearance (95% CI 0.19–0.65, P=0.001), with improved functional outcomes (P<0.05), although the assessment data were not consistent or standardized.
The evidence is insufficient to determine whether vancomycin MIC creep is a worldwide phenomenon.
The supplied background states it is unknown whether the phenomenon is worldwide or localized to specific centers.

The only data come from a single tertiary university hospital in Portugal, where MRSA isolates showed significant fluctuation in the rate with vancomycin MIC >1 mg/L over 3 years (2007: 86.2%; 2008: 93.3%; 2009: 58.8%; p=0.002), and no isolate had a MIC >2 mg/L.
Yes—older adults with cancer fell more often, with a fall rate of 33% versus 29% in those without cancer and an adjusted odds ratio of 1.16.
This rests on 862 older adults aged 65 years or older with cancer compared to 8,617 older adults without cancer from a Michigan home- and community-based waiver program.
Fall rates did not differ by cancer type or stage, and the odds of falling did not increase with time since diagnosis.

No; the evidence indicates that globulomaxillary cysts are not a distinct entity, because in 17 retrospectively analyzed cases originally diagnosed as globulomaxillary cysts, the lesions were reassigned to other entities.
The population was 12 men and 5 women aged 12–59 years with primary diagnoses of globulomaxillary cyst, compared with the international literature and reassigned to new entities.

Reclassification found 7 lateral periodontal cysts, 4 radicular cysts, 2 keratocystic odontogenic tumours, 1 adenomatoid odontogenic tumour, 1 periapical granuloma, 1 residual cyst, and 1 undefined jaw cyst.
Thus, cystic lesions in this region still occur, but the term globulomaxillary cyst is no longer considered its own entity.
Yes—women with major depression in pregnancy can be identified in population health data, but only incompletely and best through linked datasets rather than a single source.

In Western Australia from 2002–2005, 4,485 of 96,698 pregnant women (4.6%) had an antidepressant dispensing record and 3,010 (3.1%) had a depression comorbidity on a hospital admission, but only 899 pregnancies appeared in both groups (13.6% of all cases).

Data linkage identified 6,596 individual pregnancies, yet 80% of women dispensed an antidepressant had no hospital-recorded depression comorbidity, and capture-recapture estimated the true prevalence at about 16%, showing substantial under-ascertainment.
Thus, such women are identifiable in population health data, but hospital or dispensing records alone miss many cases.

The evidence is mixed: in one qualitative study, patients with knee osteoarthritis generally found colour an acceptable way to describe pain and most thought they could use it with healthcare professionals, but it did not suit all participants and concerns about interpretability and standardization were raised.

This rests on six group interviews with 17 patients with knee OA, in which the majority chose red for high-intensity pain and colours like grey or black for aching pain, while sharp pain was described with a wider selection of colours.
The majority also thought they would be able to use colour to describe their pain to healthcare professionals, although the study did not establish standardized colour meanings.
The evidence is insufficient to settle this in humans, but a canine model suggests solitary kidneys are more resistant to warm ischemia.
The authors state there are no evidence-based medicine data to critically judge solitary kidney vulnerability versus paired kidneys.

In 10 dogs with a solitary kidney versus 10 with paired kidneys subjected to 90 minutes of left renal artery occlusion, solitary-kidney dogs had only a 20% clearance decrease at 1 week and regained basal function from week 2, whereas paired-kidney dogs had more than 90% clearance decrease up to week 2 and still had a 23% reduction at 4 weeks.

Histology showed less tubular necrosis in solitary kidneys (60% at 3 days, regeneration from 1 week) than paired kidneys (90%, regeneration from 2 weeks), and proinflammatory markers were higher and more sustained in paired kidneys.
No—in this prospective study bicompartmental knee arthroplasty was not more favourable than TKA for knee muscle strength or physical performance.

Among 24 patients (31 knees) examined preoperatively and at 6 and 12 months, knee extensor and flexor torque, hamstring/quadriceps ratio, position sense, and physical performance were not significantly different between the bicompartmental and TKA groups.
Both groups improved in the 6-min walk test, while only the TKA group showed enhancement in the stair climbing test.
The groups differed in mean age (54.8 vs 65.7 years), which may limit interpretation.
Yes, concerns still exist.

In a 2010 cross-sectional observational study of 65 children younger than 6 presenting to an inner-city pediatric emergency department after the 2007 FDA warnings, 82% (53/65) of caregivers stated they would treat with cough or cold medicines, and 72% (38/53) of those incorrectly dosed the medication they desired to give.
These findings show continued use and frequent dosing errors in this population.

No—based on the supplied pilot data, sternal skin conductance is not supported as a reasonable surrogate for hot flash measurement, because the second prototype showed only 24% concordance between self-reported and device-recorded hot flashes.

In that study, women recorded hot flashes in a prospective diary while wearing SSC devices, and the first prototype yielded no analyzable skin conductance data while the second prototype had a 24% concordance rate.
Sixteen women wore the device for 5 weeks and found it acceptable, though 31% reported interference with daily activities, but this addresses acceptability rather than surrogate accuracy.

No, the evidence does not show that a history of unintended pregnancy lessens the likelihood of desiring sterilization reversal; unadjusted analysis found higher odds and adjusted analysis found no significant association.

Among 1,418 women ages 15-44 who were surgically sterile from tubal sterilization in the 2006-2010 National Survey of Family Growth, 78% had a history of at least one unintended pregnancy and 28% expressed desire for reversal.

Comparing women with versus without a history of unintended pregnancy, the unadjusted odds of desiring reversal were higher (OR 1.80, 95% CI 1.15-2.79), but after adjusting for sociodemographic factors the association was not significant (OR 1.46, 95% CI 0.91-2.34).
No—the available evidence indicates oblique views do not add diagnostic value in adolescents with suspected spondylolysis.

In a retrospective study of 50 adolescents with L5 spondylolysis without spondylolisthesis and 50 controls confirmed not to have spondylolysis, four-view radiographs (AP, lateral, and both obliques) showed no significant difference from two-view radiographs (AP and lateral) in sensitivity (0.53 vs 0.59, p=0.33) or specificity (0.94 vs 0.96, p=0.60).
Inter-rater, intra-rater, and gold-standard agreement also did not differ significantly, while four-view studies increased radiation effective dose (1.26 vs 0.72 mSv) and cost ($145 more).

Mostly yes: 91.5% (2956/3230) of multidisciplinary team (MDT) decisions in breast cancer were concordant with subsequent patient management. The study included all referrals to the breast MDT where breast cancer was diagnosed from 1 July 2009 to 30 June 2011, comprising 3230 MDT decisions relating to 705 patients. However, 4.5% (146/3230) of decisions were discordant and 4% (128/3230) had no MDT decision. Yes, in a small matched-pair study, intraoperative neuromonitoring was associated with better urogenital and anorectal functional outcomes after open total mesorectal excision.

Yes, the evidence supports that orthostatic myoclonus (OM) is a cause of unsteadiness and may be underrecognized, as it was the most frequent disorder among patients with unexplained unsteadiness/gait impairment.

Patients with platelet count ≤205 had significantly better 5-year survival than those with >205 (60.7% vs.

Yes, the evidence suggests it is feasible to maintain HIV viral load suppression over time in this resource-limited setting, since 69 of 79 patients (87.3%) on HAART had undetectable viral load.
The population was 82 HIV-infected patients diagnosed in the pre-HAART era in Buenos Aires, Argentina, of whom 79 (96.3%) were on HAART for a median of 14 years.

Bottom line: Yes, an optimistic outlook predicts better survival at advanced ages, though the evidence is strongest in women and weaker/non-significant in men.

In the Danish 1905 Cohort of 2,262 people aged 92–93 at baseline, optimistic women and men had lower univariable risk of death over 12 years than neutral counterparts (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.73–0.93 for women; HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.66–0.99 for men).

After adjustment for baseline physical and cognitive functioning and disease, optimistic women still had lower risk (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.74–0.97), whereas optimistic men showed a non-significant lower risk (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.73–1.13).

The evidence is insufficient to conclude that urinary biomarker assessment is a non-invasive approach to tubular lesions of the solitary kidney, because the passages do not explicitly state non-invasiveness or compare biomarkers with histologic tubular lesions.

In a cross-sectional study of 37 patients with solitary kidney, urinary NAG, alpha-1-microglobulin, and albuminuria were measured, with the aim of analyzing their significance in assessment of tubulointerstitial lesions of the SK.

In acquired SK, NAG increased in 60.66%, alpha-1-microglobulin in 16.66%, and albuminuria in 55.55%; in congenital SK, NAG increased in 52.63%, alpha-1-microglobulin in 5.26%, and albuminuria in 47.36%, and these biomarkers correlated inversely with eGFR.
Thus, the passages show an association between urinary biomarkers and eGFR but do not settle whether this is a non-invasive approach to tubular lesions.

Mixed: among patients undergoing LAGB with HHR, suture number and location did not significantly affect 30-day readmission, band-related reoperation, or postoperative BMI/%EWL, but they did affect OR time and LOS.
In a retrospective single-institution series of 2,301 patients, most had one suture (range 1–6; 55%), and anterior placement was most common (61%).

Yes, CA72-4 appears useful for differential diagnosis between ovarian endometrioma and epithelial ovarian cancer, based on a marked difference in serum CA72-4 values between the two groups.

Hospital stay was longer with coverage (17 days vs 13 days), but these findings are limited by the retrospective, single-center design and small sample size.
Yes, trabecular bone is related to primary stability of miniscrews.

Trabecular number, trabecular thickness, BV/TV, trabecular BMD, and total BMD correlated with insertion torque, mini-implant mobility (PTV), and pull-out strength (P≤.05).

Evidence is mixed: among high users of the smartphone insulin dose advisor (IDA), adding telemonitoring/teleconsultation did not significantly improve HbA1c compared with IDA alone (change -0.49±0.60% vs -0.52±0.73%, respectively; P=0.879).

The evidence is insufficient to say combined therapy is more effective than growth hormone or hyperbaric oxygen alone for healing left ischemic and non-ischemic colonic anastomoses.

In 80 male Wistar rats with non-ischemic or ischemic colonic anastomoses (n=10 per group), combined hyperbaric oxygen plus growth hormone increased mean bursting pressure in all groups, with a statistically significant increase in ischemic groups compared to untreated controls (p<0.05), and improvement was more evident in ischemic and normal groups treated with combined therapy.
However, the passages do not report a direct comparison of combined therapy versus growth hormone alone or hyperbaric oxygen alone.

The evidence is insufficient to conclude that the 7th TNM edition is suitable as a biological predictor in early gastric cancer, because the supplied passages report associations with clinicopathological features but no formal predictive-performance assessment.

In 1,845 patients with early gastric cancer who underwent surgery between 2005 and 2008, the study compared sixth and seventh TNM staging and found that cases upstaged from IB to IIA by the seventh edition were more significantly associated with poor differentiation, signet ring cell, diffuse and undifferentiated types, perineural invasion, larger size, and younger age.

These findings suggest the 7th edition captures some adverse biology, but they do not establish that it is suitable as a biological predictor.
The evidence is mixed: an inverse association between digoxin use and prostate cancer risk was observed, but the overall result was not statistically significant.

In a population-based case-control study of 1,001 prostate cancer cases and 942 controls aged 35-74, digoxin use was associated with a reduced odds of prostate cancer (OR 0.58, 95% CI: 0.30-1.10) after adjusting for age, race, PSA screening, and family history.

The evidence is insufficient to show that routinely collected ambulance data reduce community violence, but it suggests they could contribute by identifying assault concentrations unknown to police.

More severely injured patients, estimated by transfer to hospital, tended to be injured in places with the highest number of police-recorded crimes, supporting the potential value of ambulance data for targeting violence-prevention efforts, though no reduction outcome was measured.
Yes—most athletes with ventricular arrhythmias during an initial exercise test had far fewer ventricular arrhythmias on repeat exercise testing after a mean follow-up of 70 ± 25 months.

The study identified 192 athletes with ventricular arrhythmias from a database of 56,462, and 39 returned for repeat exercise testing (12 from the ≥3 VPB group, 21 from the couplets/NSVT group, and 6 controls).
Comparing initial versus follow-up exercise tests, most athletes who initially had VPB, ventricular couplets, or NSVT had far fewer ventricular arrhythmias at follow-up (P = 0.001).
The evidence is insufficient to conclude that the prognosis depends on the omnipresence of the allergen.

In a 2-year follow-up of 199 patients with occupational allergic contact dermatitis, total eczema clearance occurred in 22% of those allergic to a nonubiquitous allergen (epoxy) versus 10% of those allergic to ubiquitous allergens (rubber chemicals) and 0% of those with latex contact urticaria, but this difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.116).
Improvement was significantly more frequent in patients who changed jobs compared with those who did not (P = 0.01).
Thus, the passages show a non-significant trend but do not establish that omnipresence of the allergen determines prognosis.

The evidence is insufficient to establish that portable ultrasonography is accurate for Schanz pin placement in austere environments, because the supplied study is a cadaveric model and does not mention portable devices or austere settings.

In that study, 16 Schanz pins placed in bilateral femora and tibiae were measured by four examiners using ultrasonography versus direct measurement after dissection, and ultrasonography underestimated pin protrusion by an average of 10% over 5 to 18 mm (p<0.01), with proportional bias that worsened at larger protrusions.
Ultrasound correlated well and closely represented actual protrusion only in the 5 to 12 mm range, while interobserver repeatability was not statistically different (p>0.8).
Thus, the passages support potential accuracy and repeatability in a narrow cadaveric range but do not settle accuracy for austere clinical extremity fracture fixation.

The evidence is mixed: in 207 patients without any atherosclerotic disease history, there was no linear correlation between epicardial fat tissue thickness and serum paraoxonase 1, but PON1 was significantly lower when epicardial fat thickness was ≥7 mm.

Yes, the SYNTAX score predicts in-hospital outcomes in STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI, based on higher rates of no-reflow, reinfarction, and mortality in the high-score group.

In 538 STEMI patients undergoing pPCI, those with high SYNTAX score (>22) versus low (<22) had more no-reflow (41% vs 25.1%, p<0.001), greater reinfarction (9.5% vs 7.3%, p=0.037), and higher mortality (0.9% vs 0.2%, p=0.021) during hospitalization.
On multivariate analysis, SYNTAX score was an independent predictor of no-reflow (OR 1.081, 95% CI 1.032-1.133, p=0.001).

In 9,289 Oklahoma Medicaid members with epilepsy and/or psychiatric disorder, there was a prewarning upward trend of 0.01% per month in AED prescription claims, but no significant change in trend was detected during (-20.0%, 99% CI -70.0% to 30.0%, p=0.34) or after (80.0%, 99% CI -20.0% to 200.0%, p=0.03) the FDA warning period.
Stratified analyses also found no significant change in trend for any diagnostic group (epilepsy alone, epilepsy with comorbid psychiatric disorder, or psychiatric disorder alone; p>0.01).
No—local anesthesia is not needed before shoulder MR arthrography, because subcutaneous infiltration did not reduce pain compared with no anesthesia.

The study did find significant sex differences in subjective pain perception (p=.009), but this difference was equal across all three groups (p=.934).
Yes, ethnicity affects where people with cancer die, as country of birth was associated with place of death among older cancer decedents in London.

The 730-day cumulative developments of vascularization were 17%, 30%, and 40%, respectively, and the differences among these developments were not statistically significant.
No—concomitant anterior/apical repair did not improve the overactive bladder component of mixed incontinence beyond midurethral sling alone in the supplied retrospective cohort.

Among 151 women with bothersome mixed urinary incontinence, 67 underwent MUS-only and 84 underwent MUS plus anterior/apical repair, with the primary outcome being change in OAB-q Symptom Severity at 6 weeks.
OAB-q SS change scores were 30 ± 26 for MUS-only versus 25 ± 25 for MUS + AA (p = 0.20), and multivariate regression also showed no difference between cohorts.
This is retrospective and limited to 6-week follow-up, but it does not show an added OAB benefit from concomitant repair.
No—parental factors did not moderate the association between puberty and young adolescent alcohol use in this study.

Among 7,631 adolescents aged 10–14 from 231 Australian schools, the interaction of family factors (parent-adolescent emotional closeness, family conflict, parental permissiveness) with pubertal stage did not improve the fit of a two-level logistic regression model, so a main-effects model was adopted.
The significant findings were main effects of pubertal stage: boys in middle puberty and girls in advanced puberty had increased odds of recent (30-day) alcohol use.
No, the supplied evidence does not show an association between HIF1A polymorphisms and age-related macular degeneration (AMD).

In a prospective study of 87 AMD patients (45 wet, 42 dry) and 80 healthy controls, the HIF1A SNPs rs11549465 and rs11549467 showed no statistically significant difference in genotype distribution between patients and healthy subjects.
The only significant polymorphism association reported was for CFH rs1061170, not HIF1A.

The evidence is mixed: some mental health differences exist between Francophones and non-Francophones in Manitoba, but not across all indicators. Outside urban areas, Francophones had lower rates of diagnosed substance use disorder (rate ratio [RR] = 0.80; 95% CI 0.68 to 0.95) and of suicide and suicide attempts (RR = 0.59; 95% CI 0.43 to 0.79) compared with non-Francophones, but no differences were found across the province in diagnosed mood disorders, anxiety disorders, dementia, or any mental disorders after adjusting for age, sex, and geographic area. In that study, 39% reported return to play on the day of injury, and among the 44% who returned to activities at 2 weeks, 35% were symptomatic and 58% did not receive medical clearance.
At 4 weeks, 64% had returned to activities, 23% were symptomatic, and 54% received medical clearance.
The passages do not report a single overall compliance rate, but these findings indicate that many patients did not follow activity and clearance instructions.

Yes—in a retrospective case-control study, ACL reconstruction failure was associated with steeper posterior tibial slopes.
Among 20 ACLR failure cases and 20 controls selected from 238 patients followed at least 2 years, the failure group was reported to have significantly steeper medial PTS (3.5° ± 2.5° vs.
